title: SandScape-AR
summary: An augmented reality sandbox that turns depth-camera data into live elevation colours, contours, and water visuals projected onto reshaped sand.
details: The sandbox combines an Intel RealSense D435i depth camera, Raspberry Pi 4, and a projector. Changes to the physical sand surface become a live topographic visualisation.
contribution: Co-developed the AR sandbox as part of a course team. The Python pipeline uses baseline calibration, noise filtering, and adaptive smoothing to stabilise the terrain visualisation.
highlights: Depth-camera input from the Intel RealSense D435i
Live elevation colours, contour lines, and water effects
Baseline calibration and smoothing for stable projection

title: Shuttle & Passenger Scheduling
summary: A modular C++ scheduling system that matches passengers to shuttles within seat limits and a 10-minute arrival window.
details: Co-developed for SIT's Object-Oriented Programming course. The system uses SOLID principles and Strategy and Factory patterns to keep scheduling responsibilities modular.
contribution: Contributed console input and validators, file loading and saving helpers, schedule assignment and serialisation, shuttle-package validation, and strategy registration.
highlights: Passenger matching within seat limits and a 10-minute arrival window
Modular scheduling with Strategy and Factory patterns
Input validation, persistence helpers, and schedule serialisation

title: Digital Clinic Accessibility Router
summary: An accessibility-routing prototype for a simulated neighbourhood, with multi-stop routes, sheltered paths in rain, and stair-free wheelchair routing.
details: Uses Dijkstra's algorithm and a heap-based priority queue to plan walking routes for elderly and wheelchair users in a simulated neighbourhood. The interface visualises the route and breaks down its cost.
contribution: Co-developed the prototype in a six-person team. The team validated routing, accessibility settings, and interface behaviour through nine test scenarios.
highlights: Sheltered-route preferences in rain and stair-free wheelchair routing

title: Live Bus Data Integration
summary: A Python application in development that retrieves live bus metrics from transport APIs and organises them using SQL and NoSQL storage.
details: Developing a Python application that retrieves live bus metrics through external transport APIs. A hybrid SQL/NoSQL storage model is being used to organise and query the incoming data.
contribution: Developing the application and documenting API workflows and database schemas to track the system logic and support ongoing work.
highlights: Hybrid SQL and NoSQL storage model
API workflow and database schema documentation
